title: Simultaneous calibration of rotation and phase errors in a single experiment
authors: Tien D. Nguyen, Hung Q. Nguyen
abstract: In weakly anharmonic qubits, coherent control errors take two generic forms -- over/under-rotation and phase errors -- whose suppression normally requires iterated experiments. We show that, for any symmetric $π/2$ pulse in the weak-driving regime, both follow from a single parametrization, $\mathcal{X}(π/2)=Z(δ)X(π/2+ε)Z(δ)$, that ties the rotation error $ε$ and the phase error $δ$ directly to the system parameters. The parametrization enables DRAPE, a Ramsey-type protocol in which sweeping the phase-error correction reveals a crossing point that fixes both corrections at once. The phase correction is estimated with Heisenberg scaling while the rotation error saturates the standard quantum limit. We experimentally demonstrate DRAPE by calibrating a $π/2$ gate on the $|1\rangle\leftrightarrow |2\rangle$ transition of an IBM transmon, reducing the over-rotation from $0.997^\circ$ to $-0.007^\circ$ and the phase error from $2.52^\circ$ to $0.0052^\circ$ per gate, validated independently by phase- and rotation-error amplification protocols.
summary: The paper introduces the DRAPE protocol to overcome the limitations of sequential error characterization in superconducting qubits. By designing a single Ramsey-type measurement sequence, it simultaneously calibrates both rotation and phase errors ($\epsilon$ and $\delta$). This method significantly improves gate fidelity by achieving superior scaling for phase estimation compared to traditional iterative techniques.
main_problem: Coherent control errors, specifically over/under-rotation ($\epsilon$) and phase error ($\delta$), in weakly anharmonic qubits require simultaneous calibration to reach fault-tolerance thresholds.
main_result: The proposed DRAPE protocol allows for the single-shot, simultaneous calibration of both $\epsilon$ and $\delta$, achieving Heisenberg scaling for phase estimation while saturating the standard quantum limit for rotation error.
method: A Ramsey-type diagnostic sequence (DRAPE) is used to measure population probabilities $P_{|jangle}$ based on a composite unitary operator, allowing simultaneous fitting of both error parameters via Fisher information analysis.
model_or_system: The study uses weakly anharmonic qubits, experimentally demonstrated on the $|1angle \leftrightarrow |2angle$ transition of an IBM transmon superconducting qubit. The underlying physics is modeled using effective Hamiltonians derived via Schrieffer-Wolff and Magnus expansions.
key_observables: Population probabilities $P_{|jangle}$ (or $P_{|j+1angle}$) measured after the gate sequence; Fisher Information ($F_{\xi\xi}$).
important_parameters: Error parameters ($\epsilon$, $\delta$); Number of repetitions ($N$) leading to Heisenberg scaling for phase estimation.
main_assumptions: The analysis is restricted to the weak-driving regime, and derivations rely on truncations (e.g., $O((\Omega/\Delta^2)^2)$) in Hamiltonian expansions.
figures_summary: Figures numerically confirm that the Fisher information for phase ($\delta$) shows a maximum at the crossing point $ eta_0$, while rotation error ($\epsilon$) is estimated by analyzing slopes away from this point.
paper_structure: The paper first derives the coupled error parametrization, then introduces the DRAPE protocol based on measuring population probabilities. It analyzes the scaling of the Fisher information for both parameters at the optimal crossing point $ eta_0$, culminating in experimental demonstration and independent validation using established protocols (ARE/APE).
why_interesting: This work directly addresses a critical bottleneck in quantum computation: characterizing complex, coupled gate errors without resorting to slow, iterative calibration routines. The ability to achieve Heisenberg scaling for one error while maintaining high precision on another simultaneously is highly valuable.
